analyst_view.overall: Nordsjaelland (25th, 2 pts) host Panathinaikos (2nd, 9 pts): for the Danes it is close to a final in the race for the top 24, while Panathinaikos, on a long winning run in all competitions and three from three in this competition, would move close to a top-eight place; about 2,000 Greek fans are expected. Nordsjaelland beat Copenhagen 5-0 and Randers 6-1 in their last two league games, form the numbers only partly see, and report no new absentees beyond goalkeeper doubts. Panathinaikos are without Andino (now out for the season), Ounahi and Ingason (all counted), plus Pantelidis, and Greek outlets confirm centre-back Stefan de Vrij (wrist) and left-back Giorgos Kyriakopoulos (muscle) did not travel, which the numbers don't know; Palmer-Brown or Katris should partner Van Drongelen and Calabria or Christiansen cover at left-back. Austrian referee Julian Weinberger is named, and the numbers already add about 10% to cards for his record.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.7 goals, split 1.5 to 1.2, already taking off Andino, Ounahi and Ingason for Panathinaikos. Today's Greek previews confirm a reshuffled back four without de Vrij and Kyriakopoulos, with a right-back likely moved to the left, which the numbers can't see, and Nordsjaelland have scored eleven in their last two league games. I keep +6%, about 2.9 goals.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.7 corners, split evenly. Both sides like the ball and the numbers already reflect their corner records; losing Kyriakopoulos takes some crossing from the left for Panathinaikos while Nordsjaelland may attack more down that side, which roughly cancels, so I stay at about 9.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.1 cards, already raised about 10% for Panathinaikos' recent bookings and 10% for referee Weinberger's record (5.2 a game). A makeshift Panathinaikos defence may have to foul more against Nordsjaelland's quick attack, but that is a guess on top of an already high figure, so I stay at about 5.1.

shots.text: The numbers say 26.0 shots, already raised 5% for Nordsjaelland's recent volume. Nordsjaelland chasing a must-win game at home should push that up, but a Panathinaikos side keeping the ball on the artificial pitch can slow the game, so I stay at about 26.0.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 shots on target, already nudged up for both sides' recent accuracy. Nordsjaelland's sharp league finishing and a Panathinaikos defence confirmed without de Vrij and Kyriakopoulos, neither of which the numbers can see, point slightly higher: +4% gives about 10.0.
